Everyone wants the financial answers. You're the one expected to have them.

You've gathered the data, checked the calculations, and prepared the reports. Then someone asks how the business is actually doing, and you need to bring everything into one clear explanation.

I built my Financial Performance & Cash Flow Power BI Kit to help organize that reporting work: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595413257/power-bi-financial-dashboard-template-13

Preparing financial reports can feel like assembling a puzzle from several different places.

Revenue is in one report, profitability is in another, and the cash forecast lives somewhere else. Each piece matters, but connecting them takes additional work when someone needs an explanation.

Try identifying the three financial views you use most often in reporting meetings. Could you organize them into a consistent framework that makes the connections easier to follow?

There's real responsibility behind the financial numbers people present in meetings.

Hiring, spending, investment, and operating decisions can all depend on understanding performance and available cash. Clear reporting helps give those conversations a stronger foundation.

My Financial Performance & Cash Flow Power BI Kit brings performance, entity comparisons, and cash forecasting together: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595413257/power-bi-financial-dashboard-template-13

Walking into a financial reporting meeting feels different when you've already explored the questions people are likely to ask.

How are revenue and margins trending? Which operating entities are driving results? What does the next quarter's cash position look like? Having those answers organized can make the discussion more productive.

Before your next meeting, try preparing a short explanation for each of those three areas. Where do you still need more context?

You shouldn't have to rebuild every financial reporting foundation from scratch.

A reusable framework gives you a starting point for organizing performance trends, entity comparisons, and cash forecasts. You can then adapt the structure to the questions your business needs answered.

That's why my Financial Performance & Cash Flow Power BI Kit includes three editable report pages and documentation: https://garrettsdevdesk.etsy.com/listing/4595413257/power-bi-financial-dashboard-template-13

Anyone who's responsible for financial reporting knows that preparing accurate numbers is only part of the job.

You also need to explain what changed, answer follow-up questions, and help people understand what the results might mean for the business. That responsibility can make even a routine reporting meeting feel demanding.

For finance professionals and business owners, what's the hardest part of presenting financial results to other people?
